# rzv-opencode-plugin agent guide

Runzivo-wide rules: [rzv-business/operating-policy.md](https://github.com/Runzivo/rzv-business/blob/main/operating-policy.md) (local checkout: ../rzv-business/operating-policy.md). This file adds only plugin guidance.

- The plugin only runs the `rzv` CLI and `ssh`. Sandbox logic belongs in `rzv` in Runzivo/rzv-cli; no API calls, tokens or AI keys here.
- Keep runtime dependencies to `@opencode-ai/plugin`. `src/` ships as TypeScript; there is no build step.
- Run the checks in docs/testing.md on every change, and the live test before a tag.
- The repository is public: no internal hostnames, inventory, secrets or unreleased plans.

# Runzivo Sandboxes for OpenCode Create and manage [Runzivo](https://runzivo.dev) sandboxes from inside [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). A sandbox is an isolated Linux microVM with your files in `/workspace`. OpenCode can create one, run commands in it over SSH, show what it costs, put it to sleep, wake it and delete it. Compute is charged per running minute from your Runzivo workspace credits; there is no separate plan. [![CI](https://github.com/Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin)](https://github.com/Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin/releases/latest) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Runzivo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runzivo-sandboxes-0B0F14)](https://runzivo.dev/sandboxes/) The plugin only runs the `rzv` CLI on your machine. It makes no API calls of its own, stores no tokens, and never reads or uploads your code. ## Requirements - OpenCode 1.19.5 or later - OpenSSH and a Runzivo account with a workspace that has credit - The `rzv` CLI 0.26.0 or later, signed in: ```sh curl -fsSL https://runzivo.dev/downloads/rzv/install.sh | sh rzv login ``` ## Install Add the plugin to `opencode.json` in your project, or to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` for every project: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["github:Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin#v0.1.0"] } ``` Restart OpenCode. It installs the plugin from GitHub at that tag. The plugin finds `rzv` in `RZV_BIN`, then `PATH`, then `~/.local/bin/rzv`. ## Use Type a command, or just ask OpenCode ("start a 4 vCPU Runzivo sandbox and run the tests there"). | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `/rzv-create [size] [lifetime]` | Create a sandbox, wait until it runs, write the `.rzv` SSH alias | | `/rzv-status [id]` | Status, expiry, time left, run time and credits used | | `/rzv-connect ` | Write the SSH alias and show `ssh .rzv` | | `/rzv-exec ` | Run a command in the sandbox over SSH | | `/rzv-sleep ` / `/rzv-wake ` | Stop or start the sandbox | | `/rzv-delete ` | Delete it and all its files, after you confirm | Sandboxes the plugin creates are named `opencode--`. Details: [Tools and commands](docs/usage.md). ## Documentation | Page | What it covers | | --- | --- | | [Tools and commands](docs/usage.md) | Every tool, its options, lifetime and billing | | [Security](docs/security.md) | What runs where, keys, permissions | | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Errors and how to fix them | | [Testing](docs/testing.md) | Unit tests and the live end-to-end test | | [Releasing](docs/releasing.md) | Versions, tags, npm and the OpenCode ecosystem list | MIT licensed ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). The `rzv` CLI and the Runzivo service keep their own licenses.

# Changelog

## 0.1.0

- First release: tools and slash commands to create a Runzivo sandbox, show status and credits, write the SSH alias, run commands over SSH, stop, start and delete (with confirmation), all through the `rzv` CLI 0.26.0 or later.

# Releasing

1. Update `version` in `package.json`, the tag in the README install snippet, and `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Merge to `main` with the `check` status green.
3. Run the live test in [testing](testing.md) against `main`.
4. Tag and release:

   ```sh
   git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z
   gh release create vX.Y.Z --notes-file <notes>
   ```

5. Run the live test again with `PLUGIN_SPEC=github:Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin#vX.Y.Z`.

## Install channels

- GitHub (current): `"plugin": ["github:Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin#vX.Y.Z"]`. OpenCode installs it with npm's installer, without running install scripts, so `src/` ships as TypeScript and OpenCode loads it directly.
- npm: not published yet. When it is, the package name is `opencode-runzivo` and users write `"plugin": ["opencode-runzivo"]`.

## OpenCode ecosystem list

The plugin is listed on [opencode.ai/docs/ecosystem](https://opencode.ai/docs/ecosystem) through a pull request to `packages/web/src/content/docs/ecosystem.mdx` in [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode). Update the entry only if the repository moves.

Back to the [README](../README.md).

# Security

## What the plugin does

It runs the `rzv` CLI and `ssh` on your machine, with fixed argument lists and no shell. It makes no network calls of its own, stores nothing, and does not read, copy or upload files from your project. The source is two short TypeScript files in `src/`.

## Your Runzivo sign-in

`rzv` keeps your sign-in in its own owner-only credentials file. The plugin never sees the token, never prints it and never passes it to a sandbox. Every action uses Runzivo's workspace roles: you can only see or change sandboxes in workspaces where you have `sandboxes:read` or `sandboxes:write`.

## SSH

`rzv sandboxes ssh-config <id> --write` writes `~/.ssh/rzv/<id>.conf`, included from `~/.ssh/config`. Connections use a short-lived user certificate, strict host verification against the Runzivo host CA, and no agent or X11 forwarding. The sandbox has no public SSH port; `rzv` relays the connection.

## AI provider keys

The plugin bundles no AI keys and never touches yours. OpenCode on your machine talks to your provider as usual. If you run an AI tool inside the sandbox, send its key over SSH into a mode 600 file in your home directory, for example:

```sh
<password-manager-command> | ssh <id>.rzv 'umask 077; cat > ~/.openai.key'
```

Never put keys in `/workspace`, in a `rzv_sandbox_exec` command, or in `rzv sandboxes exec --env`: commands can end up in logs and shell history.

## Commands the agent runs

`rzv_sandbox_exec` runs whatever command the agent picks, inside the sandbox only. Like OpenCode's own `bash` tool it is allowed by default. To review each one, set `"permission": {"rzv_sandbox_exec": "ask"}`. Deletes always ask unless you allow them.

Back to the [README](../README.md).

# Testing

## Checks (CI)

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx tsc --noEmit
npm test
shellcheck scripts/*.sh
```

The unit tests in `test/` cover finding `rzv`, the version check, sandbox names, error messages and running commands without a shell. They use a fake `rzv` and never reach Runzivo.

## Live end-to-end test

`scripts/20-shared-e2e.sh` drives OpenCode itself: each step is one `opencode run` turn that calls a plugin tool, and `rzv` checks the result. It covers create, exec, status and credits, stop, start, that `/workspace` survives the stop, a refused delete without approval, and the approved delete. A trap deletes the sandbox if any step fails.

```sh
OPENCODE_BIN=<path to opencode 1.19.5> OPENAI_KEY_FILE=<mode 600 key file> \
  E2E_DIR=<empty directory> scripts/20-shared-e2e.sh
```

It refuses to run unless `rzv whoami` shows `Environment: shared`, uses OpenCode with its own config directories under `E2E_DIR`, and checks that the key does not appear in the saved output. Use the cheapest model your provider offers (default `openai/gpt-5-nano`).

Run it before every release. Set `PLUGIN_SPEC=github:Runzivo/rzv-opencode-plugin#vX.Y.Z` to test the published tag.

Back to the [README](../README.md).

# Troubleshooting

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `The rzv CLI was not found` | Install it with `curl -fsSL https://runzivo.dev/downloads/rzv/install.sh \| sh`, or set `RZV_BIN` to its path. Restart OpenCode. |
| `This plugin needs rzv 0.26.0 or later` | Run the install command again to update `rzv`. |
| `Sign in with rzv login first` or `Your sign-in has expired` | Run `rzv login` in a terminal. The next tool call works without restarting OpenCode. |
| `credit_exhausted` | The workspace is out of credit. Add credit in the Runzivo portal, then start the sandbox again. |
| `sandbox_capacity_busy` or `no_capacity` | No free capacity for that size right now. Try again in a few minutes, or pick a smaller size. |
| `sandbox_limit_reached` | The workspace runs its maximum number of sandboxes. Stop or delete one (`/rzv-status` lists them). |
| `size_unavailable` | That size is not offered. `rzv sandboxes sizes` lists the ones you can use. |
| `sandbox_expired` | The lifetime ended. Create a new sandbox. |
| `SSH to <id>.rzv failed` | The sandbox must be running: `/rzv-wake <id>`. Check `ssh -V` works. |
| Delete says permission rejected | You declined, or you used `opencode run` without `--auto`. Run it again and approve. |
| The tools do not appear | Check the `plugin` entry, then restart OpenCode. `opencode debug config` shows the loaded commands. |

A sandbox you forget about still stops and is deleted at the end of its lifetime. `rzv sandboxes list` shows every sandbox in the workspace, and `rzv sandboxes delete <id>` removes one.

Back to the [README](../README.md).

# Tools and commands

The plugin adds seven tools that OpenCode's agent can call, and a slash command for each. The commands are short prompts that ask the agent to call the tool, so they use one model turn. A command or `permission` rule you define yourself with the same name wins.

| Tool | rzv command it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `rzv_sandbox_create` | `rzv sandboxes create`, then `rzv sandboxes ssh-config <id> --write` |
| `rzv_sandbox_status` | `rzv sandboxes get <id>` or `rzv sandboxes list` |
| `rzv_sandbox_connect` | `rzv sandboxes ssh-config <id> --write` |
| `rzv_sandbox_exec` | `ssh <id>.rzv <command>` |
| `rzv_sandbox_stop` | `rzv sandboxes stop <id>` |
| `rzv_sandbox_start` | `rzv sandboxes start <id>` |
| `rzv_sandbox_delete` | `rzv sandboxes delete <id>`, after you approve |

Every call uses your current `rzv` profile and selected workspace. Set `RZV_PROFILE` or run `rzv workspaces select <workspace>` before you start OpenCode to change them.

## Create

Options: `size` (`2vcpu-8gb` default, `4vcpu-16gb`, `8vcpu-32gb`, `16vcpu-64gb`), `lifetime` (`8h` default, `12h`, `24h`), `disk_gib` (5 to 64) and `name`. `rzv sandboxes sizes` shows what your workspace can use. The tool waits up to five minutes for the sandbox to run.

## Connect and run commands

`rzv_sandbox_exec` runs one command through the SSH alias with OpenSSH in batch mode (default timeout 300 seconds, at most 3600) and returns its output and exit status. For an interactive shell, run `ssh <id>.rzv` in a terminal, or `rzv sandboxes ssh <id>`.

## Sleep, wake and lifetime

Stop ends running processes and the compute charge. Files in `/workspace` stay; keep your work there or push it. A sandbox lives 8, 12 or 24 hours, even while stopped; 12h and 24h are offered only where Runzivo has turned them on. The timer starts when the sandbox first runs. At the end it stops for good and its files are deleted. It cannot be extended.

## Cost

`rzv_sandbox_status` shows run time and credits used so far. A 2 vCPU sandbox costs one equivalent minute per running minute; 4, 8 and 16 vCPU cost 2x, 4x and 8x. A stopped sandbox costs nothing. Prices: [runzivo.dev](https://runzivo.dev).

## Delete

OpenCode asks before it deletes. `opencode run` without `--auto` refuses the delete. To skip the question, set `"permission": {"rzv_sandbox_delete": "allow"}`. An agent whose own `permission` allows every tool also skips it.
